description: A 4HP LFO with four waveform outputs, pulse-width and shape modulation, sync in and out, and an n-shot mode that runs a set number of cycles per sync pulse

params.text: Sets the rate, from 0.0039Hz fully counter-clockwise to 1024Hz fully clockwise, and 2Hz at the default position
Attenuates and inverts the frequency CV between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%, so that jack does nothing until you turn it
Chooses whether the outputs run from 0V upwards in the U position or centred on 0V in the B position
Sets how wide the output span is, from 0V for a flat output to 10V at the far right
Sets the pulse width, from 1% counter-clockwise to 99% clockwise, at half width in the centre
Shapes the waveforms, sharpening their peaks counter-clockwise and rounding them clockwise; the square instead morphs into a triangle counter-clockwise and into a saw clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the RNG input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Attenuates and inverts the PWM input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Attenuates and inverts the MOD input between -100% and +100%, and comes up at 0%
Turns n-shot mode on, so that each sync pulse runs the number of cycles set on the menu and then holds the outputs at a fixed level

inputs.text: Every volt here doubles the rate and every negative volt halves it, after the trim knob; a polyphonic signal here gives every output the same number of channels, each running at its own rate
Adds its voltage to the span set by the RNG knob, a volt of input widening the span by a volt once the trim knob is up
Moves the pulse width, 5V covering half the knob's travel once the trim knob is up
Moves the shaping, 10V covering the knob's full travel once the trim knob is up
A rising edge restarts the cycle, or reverses its direction when the menu is set to soft sync; a polyphonic signal here syncs each channel on its own

outputs.text: The square, high for the part of the cycle set by the pulse width and low for the rest, morphing towards a triangle or a saw as MOD is turned
The triangle, rising for the first quarter of the cycle and falling to the bottom at three quarters
The falling saw, starting at the top of the range and dropping to the bottom over one cycle
The sine, spanning the range over one cycle
Fires a 1ms trigger when a sync pulse arrives and when a cycle ends, with as many channels as the frequency input has

notes: the module stops calculating when neither a waveform output nor the sync output is patched, and the green phase light stops flashing with it
with nothing patched into the frequency jack, its normal is the sine output of this same LFO, so turning the frequency trim knob off centre makes the LFO modulate its own rate
in n-shot mode nothing runs until a sync pulse arrives; each new pulse restarts the count even if the previous run has not finished
menu: Pulse-width mode: All waveforms, Square only — chooses whether the pulse-width control warps the phase of every waveform or only sets the width of the square
Pulse-width range: 1% to 99%, 5% to 95%, 10% to 90%, 15% to 85%, 20% to 80%, 25% to 75% — narrows what the pulse-width knob covers end to end
Invert (all) waveforms — flips all four waveforms within the range, and lights a small red mark above the output jacks
Sync-mode: Hard-sync, Soft-sync — hard sync restarts the cycle at a sync pulse, soft sync reverses the direction the phase runs in
Send sync-out: Both on sync-in and phase-end, Only on sync-in, Only on phase-end — chooses what fires the sync output
Value after n-shot: Keep last, Zero (default), Center, Min, Max — sets what the waveform outputs hold once the counted cycles have run
n-shot cycles — sets how many full cycles one sync pulse runs, from 1 up to 32
Phase/frequency-lights: Disabled, Enabled — turns off the green light that flashes at the start of each cycle
LFO rate chaos — picks a new random speed for each cycle, up to a tenth or ten times the dialled rate at 100%, and is 0% for a steady rate
Clipping range — clamps every output to the range chosen, -12V to 12V unless you change it, and Off lets the output run to any voltage
Process quality: Audio, High, Balanced, Low, Very low — sets how often the module runs its algorithm, from every cycle down to every 256th; below Balanced a 1ms trigger can be missed
Auto select process quality — picks the process quality from the dialled-in rate and from which ports are patched, and greys out the manual choice while it is on
Trigger-high detect-level — sets the voltage at which an incoming trigger counts as high, 1V or more unless you change it
Trigger-low detect-level — sets the voltage an incoming trigger must fall back below before the next one is counted, under 0.1V unless you change it
Trigger-high output-level — sets the voltage a trigger pulse carries during its 1ms high phase, 10V unless you change it
Trigger-low output-level — sets the voltage a trigger output carries between pulses, 0V unless you change it
